title: Adding min()/max()/sum()/avg() aggregates wrapped the caller-supplied column name in sqlalchemy.text() with no check that it is a real model field, so a crafted column string injects SQL into the aggregate query.

findings.explanation: The diff does not contain any SQL query construction code. All changes are related to ORM model definitions, decorators, field configurations, and helper functions. No user input is being concatenated or interpolated into SQL queries. The codebase uses the `ormar` ORM and `databases`/`sqlalchemy` libraries which handle parameterized queries internally.

The diff does not introduce any endpoint handlers, access control logic, or authorization checks. The changes consist of: (1) adding new signal decorators (pre/post relation add/remove), (2) adding field configuration options (orders_by, related_orders_by), (3) extracting validation logic into a helper function, and (4) updating version numbers and exports. None of these changes touch authentication, authorization, or resource ownership validation code. There are no user-controlled identifiers being used to fetch resources without ownership checks.
